w: Bristol Zoo drew crowds through its Clifton gates for 186 years - gorillas and golden lion tamarins on the lake islands, aye-ayes and quolls found in no other UK zoo - before closing for good on 3 September 2022, its animals rehomed to a site off the M5. The grounds are being redeveloped for housing.
s: 186 years of gorillas and aye-ayes, closed for good in 2022
_facts: Opened in Clifton and ran for more than 186 years before closing on 3 September 2022
Held rare species including aye-ayes, quolls and Livingstone's fruit bats, seen at no other UK zoo
Lake islands housed gorillas, golden lion and golden-headed lion tamarins, gibbons and squirrel monkeys
Animals rehomed to the Wild Place Project site near the M5; the Clifton site is being redeveloped for housing

w: Built in the 1970s under Vatican II's fresh liturgical rules, Clifton Cathedral holds a rare distinction: the only Catholic church from that unloved decade to win Grade II* listing, awarded in 2000. It was also the first cathedral designed to the new post-Vatican II guidelines - a concrete gamble that paid off.
s: The only 1970s Catholic church in England with Grade II* listing
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Clifton, seat of the Bishop of Clifton
Built in the 1970s, the first cathedral anywhere designed under the new liturgical guidelines of the Second Vatican Council
A 2014 study found it the only Catholic church built in the 1970s to hold Grade II* listed status
